title: Completeness and the actual completion unit after ordinary open restriction
statement: Fix independent site and coefficient universes, a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, an open immersion j:U→X with ell invertible on residue fields of both schemes, and the section-normalized completed-coefficient open operations o. For every quotient-tower complete unbounded derived object H on X [def-weil-derived-complete], the ordinary exact open restriction j*H is quotient-tower complete on U and the actual normalized completion unit [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] at j*H is invertible. This concerns the given ordinary restriction functor, without choosing a reconstruction equivalence or an arbitrary comparison isomorphism.

proof.text: View the open immersion as an immersion. The fixed coefficient maps, normalized by their finite quotient projections, identify ordinary localized restriction with the actual ringed-site inverse image. On one good representative these identifications are the pure-tensor identifications and carry its quotient transitions and augmentation to the corresponding target data.

proof.text: Exact open restriction preserves countable products, so applying it to the source augmented Roos triangle gives the target quotient triangle and proves completeness. The actual completion comparison identifies its unit on the same representative with the quotient augmentation. The immersion comparison identifies this very map with the completion of the restricted source. Its invertibility transports along representative isomorphisms by naturality. This establishes invertibility of the actual target completion unit, rather than merely existence of an isomorphism.

theorem openRestrictionComplete
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ x : U, Invertible (l : U.residueField x)] :
    ∀ H, complete l E X H →
      complete l E U ((star l E j o).obj H) ∧
      IsIso ((IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E U none).app
        ((star l E j o).obj H))
